The "actual" figure of 15.4% reflects the change in GDP for the current quarter compared with the previous one, annualized, while the "previous" 14.9% reading captures the change recorded in the prior quarter versus the one before it. This subtle increase suggests that the underlying momentum in Israel's economy has strengthened, rather than plateaued, as the year progresses. The consecutive quarters of double-digit annualized growth underscore a period of exceptional economic performance. title: Romanian F-16s shoot down two drones over Black Sea, NATO council to meet Tuesday

For energy and freight markets, back-to-back drone incidents near Romania's coast raise the risk of higher war-risk insurance costs and caution among operators using western Black Sea routes. Tuesday's NATO council meeting is the next catalyst: a firmer collective response could extend risk aversion, while an outcome framed as containment may let the euro stabilise once deeper liquidity returns. --- EUR marked lower: Monday open indicative forex prices, 19 October 2026 --- Romania has now had to put fighter jets in the air to protect its own Black Sea airspace, turning a regional shipping threat into an issue NATO will take up on Tuesday.

The real test comes with the European open: French government bond spreads over Bunds and the euro's performance against the US dollar will show whether the weekend headlines are being priced as a lasting political and fiscal risk or as a passing shock. Tuesday's NATO council meeting is a further event risk for the euro. On the Australian side, Kent's remarks offer the only scheduled domestic catalyst, and anything read as dovish would blunt the Aussie's gains. --- Earlier: EUR update, France riots: 2,400 arrested as cost-of-living protests turn to looting and arson US threatens EU with devastating retaliation if Brussels curbs Starlink spectrum access Romanian F-16s shoot down two drones over Black Sea, NATO council to meet Tuesday --- The Australian dollar is winning against the euro mostly by default, as Europe brings riots, drones and a trade threat to the Monday open.
